subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding raw Codex PostToolUse strings?
rationale: The code has two plausible sources for the event: upstream native PostToolUse is synchronous but string-shaped today, while app-server completion has structured command data but is currently treated as telemetry and suppressed behind the native relay.

options.title: Canonical OpenClaw Structured Payload
options.body: Use OpenClaw's app-server command completion data, or an equivalent normalized adapter, as the public Codex-native hook payload and keep duplicate suppression explicit.

options.title: Wait For Upstream Codex Shape
options.body: Coordinate with upstream Codex for structured PostToolUse command results and keep the current raw relay until that contract exists.

options.title: Document Raw String Semantics
options.body: Declare the current raw Codex PostToolUse string as the supported behavior and treat richer command metadata as a separate future feature.

recommendation.title: Canonical OpenClaw Structured Payload
recommendation.body: Use OpenClaw's app-server command completion data, or an equivalent normalized adapter, as the public Codex-native hook payload and keep duplicate suppression explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the plugin hook API contract introduced around prior tool-result middleware work.
